rituals.name: REPLY DELAY ROULETTE
rituals.goal: One slow reply, five possible universes.
rituals.mission: One slow reply, five possible universes.
rituals.rule: Guess how many non-personal explanations you can produce before your brain returns to “they’re upset with me.”
rituals.one_rule: Guess how many non-personal explanations you can produce before your brain returns to “they’re upset with me.”

rituals.twist: Notice how much certainty the personal explanation loses once alternatives occupy the wheel.
rituals.mindBend: A slow reply is a lousy relationship detective.
rituals.mind_bend: A slow reply is a lousy relationship detective.
rituals.why: A delayed reply contains very little information about motive.
rituals.reveal: A delayed reply contains very little information about motive.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Let this pass create possibilities, not excuses. Keep direct words, consent, patterns of behaviour and your own boundaries in the picture. The result is a working perspective, not proof that the opposite story is true.

rituals.name: SAME TEXT, THREE VOICES
rituals.goal: Text messages arrive without vocal cords.
rituals.mission: Text messages arrive without vocal cords.
rituals.rule: Guess which reading changes your reaction most: warm, bored, irritated.

rituals.mindBend: Your brain can hear a tone that was never actually sent.
rituals.mind_bend: Your brain can hear a tone that was never actually sent.

rituals.reveal: Text carries words; tone is partly reconstructed by the reader.

rituals.name: RELATIONSHIP LEDGER
rituals.goal: One awkward moment is trying to buy the whole company.
rituals.mission: One awkward moment is trying to buy the whole company.
rituals.rule: Guess how large this event looks beside ten ordinary interactions from the same relationship.
rituals.one_rule: Guess how large this event looks beside ten ordinary interactions from the same relationship.
rituals.play: Name the awkward event. Rapidly list up to ten other real interactions—neutral, kind, boring, mixed, anything true. Don’t force positives.
rituals.twist: Watch the single event move from “the relationship” to “one item in the ledger.”
rituals.mindBend: One awkward message does not automatically revoke your friendship licence.
rituals.mind_bend: One awkward message does not automatically revoke your friendship licence.
rituals.why: Salient moments feel statistically larger than they are.
rituals.reveal: Salient moments feel statistically larger than they are.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the naming step on the interpretation, not the other person's rights or limits. A kinder explanation does not cancel a clear no, repeated harm or needed distance. The result is a working perspective, not proof that the opposite story is true.

rituals.name: STRANGER MEMORY TEST
rituals.goal: How closely are people really studying you?
rituals.mission: How closely are people really studying you?
rituals.rule: Guess how many details you remember about the last stranger you passed.
rituals.one_rule: Guess how many details you remember about the last stranger you passed.
rituals.play: Think of the last stranger you saw. Without cheating, recall their shoes, hair, facial expression and one flaw. Count what you genuinely remember.
rituals.twist: Compare that memory with how closely you imagine strangers are tracking your details.
rituals.mindBend: You are highly visible to yourself.
rituals.mind_bend: You are highly visible to yourself.
rituals.why: People are usually the centre of their own attention, just as you are of yours.
rituals.reveal: People are usually the centre of their own attention, just as you are of yours.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Let the memory/imagery pass create possibilities, not excuses. Keep direct words, consent, patterns of behaviour and your own boundaries in the picture. The result is a working perspective, not proof that the opposite story is true.

rituals.name: COMPLIMENT NO-RETURN POLICY
rituals.goal: For ten seconds, compliments are non-refundable.
rituals.mission: For ten seconds, compliments are non-refundable.
rituals.rule: Guess how quickly you will feel the urge to explain why the compliment does not count.
rituals.one_rule: Guess how quickly you will feel the urge to explain why the compliment does not count.
rituals.play: Recall or receive one genuine compliment. Your only allowed response is “thank you.” No joke, discount, counterexample, explanation or compliment-back for 10 sec.
rituals.twist: Catch the exact urge to return the positive information.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes praise feels wrong because your self-image has an outdated returns policy.
rituals.mind_bend: Sometimes praise feels wrong because your self-image has an outdated returns policy.
rituals.why: The discomfort may be the old self-story defending itself, not proof the compliment is false.
rituals.reveal: The discomfort may be the old self-story defending itself, not proof the compliment is false.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use the simple thank-you only for a genuine, welcome compliment. You do not need to accept praise, contact or attention that feels inappropriate, unsafe or boundary-crossing.

rituals.mind_bend: You can do your job well without secretly taking over theirs.

rituals.mechanism_fingerprint: Populate apparently composed others with plausible hidden internal states to correct private-self versus public-other asymmetry.
rituals.ritualText:
PLAY TIME
70 sec

GAME
THE QUIET ROOM MAY BE NERVOUS

GOAL
A calm-looking room can contain a lot of private panic.

ONE RULE
Guess how many people in a social situation might also be managing nerves invisibly.

PLAY
Picture the room. For three people, add one hidden internal possibility that would not show on their face: uncertainty, boredom, self-consciousness, tiredness, wanting to leave.

TWIST
Check if you still look uniquely uncomfortable.

MIND BEND
You may be measuring your backstage against a room full of front stages.

SAFETY
PAUSE
Let the mental image create possibilities, not excuses. Keep direct words, consent, patterns of behaviour and your own boundaries in the picture. The result is a working perspective, not proof that the opposite story is true.

rituals.name: THREE SIGNALS OF 'I GET YOU'
rituals.goal: People often remember whether they felt understood before they remember your brilliant advice.
rituals.mission: People often remember whether they felt understood before they remember your brilliant advice.
rituals.rule: Guess which signal is missing: understood, validated, cared for.
rituals.one_rule: Guess which signal is missing: understood, validated, cared for.

rituals.twist: Notice how the response feels different from jumping to solutions.
rituals.mindBend: Connection often begins with 'you make sense to me,' not 'here is the fix.'
rituals.mind_bend: Connection often begins with 'you make sense to me,' not 'here is the fix.'
